text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as refineries operate at high capacity (95.7%) while oil inventories remain elevated at 694 million barrels. When refineries are running full but storage is full, margins compress—refiners make less profit per barrel processed because supply outpaces demand, forcing prices down. The stock has been sliding steadily since mid-November alongside this inventory buildup.

The recent climate talks collapse, which rejected language on phasing out fossil fuels, might have offered a headline tailwind for oil stocks, but the data suggests it was overwhelmed by the structural refining headwind: too much crude in tanks and refineries already maxed out on throughput, leaving limited pricing power.
